title: Modern CSS Mastery
tagline: Write CSS you can predict: the cascade, modern layout, color and motion, explained from the browser's side.
description: Most CSS frustration comes from guessing. This course replaces guessing with the rules the browser actually follows: how the cascade picks a winner, why a flex item refuses to shrink, what a container query measures, and which animations cost a frame. You learn the 2026 toolkit (layers, nesting, :has(), subgrid, container queries, oklch(), view transitions) and when each one earns its place.

You refine one real page the whole way through: the schedule for Waypoint Conf 2026, with session cards, a speaker grid, track filters, right-to-left support and a dark mode. Almost every lesson ends with a hands-on exercise checked in a real browser, and every support claim is matched against Baseline so you know what you can ship today.
audience: Developers who already write CSS every week and want to stop fighting it, from career switchers to juniors filling gaps.
prerequisites: Comfortable with HTML and basic CSS (selectors, the box model, flexbox basics) and able to read a little JavaScript.
learnItems: Predict which declaration wins, and control it with @layer
Build components with custom properties, nesting and :has()
Lay out pages with flexbox, grid, subgrid and intrinsic sizing
Make components respond to their container, not the viewport
Ship fluid, RTL-ready, accessible themes with oklch() and light-dark()
Animate with view transitions and scroll timelines, cheaply and kindly
